data.description:

Align recognized for executive leadership, investor relations and investor engagement in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector

The 2026 awards mark Align’s fourth recognition in five years in the Extel All-America Executive Team rankings

TEMPE, Ariz. & SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Align Technology, Inc. (“Align”) (Nasdaq: ALGN), a leading global medical device company that designs, manufactures, and sells the Invisalign® System of clear aligners, iTero™ intraoral scanners, and exocad™ CAD/CAM software for digital orthodontics and restorative dentistry, today announced recognition in the 2026 All-America Executive Team rankings published by Extel Insights (formerly Institutional Investor Research), which evaluates the quality of investor relations programs, leadership, and governance as voted on by the buy- and sell-side analyst community. In the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector, Align earned first- and second-place rankings across three Large-Cap award categories – Best CEO, Best IR Program, and Best Investor Day – in both the Combined and Buy-side results. The 2026 awards mark Align’s fourth recognition in five years in the Extel All-America Executive Team rankings, reflecting the company’s longstanding commitment to transparent disclosure, meaningful investor engagement, and ongoing dialogue with shareholders and analysts.

2026 Extel All-America Executive Team Award Categories and Named Winners:

  • Best CEO:
    Joseph Hogan, President and Chief Executive Officer, ranked #2 in both the Combined, Large-Cap and Buy-side, Large-Cap results in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector.
  • Best IR Program:
    Align’s Investor Relations Program ranked #2 in the Combined, Large-Cap results and #1 in the Buy-side, Large-Cap results in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector.
  • Best Investor Day:
    Align’s Investor Day ranked #1 in both the Combined, Large-Cap and Buy-side, Large-Cap results in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector.

Commenting on Align’s recognition in Extel’s All-America Executive Team rankings, Shirley Stacy, Align Technology vice president, finance, corporate communications and IRO said, “We’re grateful for this recognition from the investment community and proud of the work our teams do every day to provide clear, consistent and meaningful investor communications. That work is truly a team effort, bringing together our communications team and colleagues across legal, finance, clinical, and marketing whose expertise and partnership are essential to our investor relations efforts. Our focus is on helping investors fully understand our strategy, performance, long-term opportunities, and the potential of our business through transparent disclosure, thoughtful engagement, and ongoing dialogue. That commitment is especially important during dynamic and challenging market periods, when clear communication and accessibility matter most. We remain focused on continuing to earn the trust and confidence of our investors.”

In 2025, Align earned the Most Honored Company distinction, with its Board of Directors and Investor Relations Program each ranked first in the Large-Cap category and among the top 10 in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector. In 2023, Align ranked third for Best IR Team and placed fourth on the Most Honored Company list, with its investor relations program highly rated for credibility, responsiveness, and market knowledge. In 2022, Align’s executive team and IR program received top-tier recognition, including first- and third-place rankings for CEO, CFO, and IR professionals, and second place for the overall IR program. These achievements were especially notable during the pandemic era, underscoring Align’s resilience and dedication to transparent communications.

Survey Methodology:

The All-America Executive Team rankings are based on comprehensive feedback from buy-side analysts, money managers, and sell-side researchers at securities firms and financial institutions, evaluating companies on leadership quality, investor relations programs, and engagement strategies. Extel asks voters to name the best chief executive officers, chief financial officers, and investor relations professionals at the companies in their coverage universes.

About Extel

For over 50 years, Extel (formerly Institutional Investor Research) has offered highly respected proprietary benchmark research and rankings, providing independent feedback on the sell-side and corporate performance; Extel aims to be the first-choice independent validation source of qualitative market intelligence for all three sides of the investment community and has a global presence spanning Europe, Emerging EMEA, Asia Pacific, North America and Latin America.

Align Technology designs and manufactures the Invisalign® System, the most advanced clear aligner system in the world, iTero™ intraoral scanners and services, and exocad™ CAD/CAM software. These technology building blocks enable enhanced digital orthodontic and restorative workflows to improve patient outcomes and practice efficiencies for over 307 thousand doctor customers and is key to accessing Align’s 600 million consumer market opportunity worldwide. Over the past 29 years, Align has helped doctors treat approximately 24.2 million patients with the Invisalign System and is driving the evolution in digital dentistry through the Align Digital Platform™, our integrated suite of unique, proprietary technologies and services delivered as a seamless, end-to-end solution for patients and consumers, orthodontists and GP dentists, and lab/partners. Celebrating National STEM Day on Nov. 8 by Helping Students Pursue STEM Careers

Link to B-roll video and soundbites of STEM recipients

OAKLAND, Calif., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The PG&E Corporation Foundation (PG&E Foundation) awarded $327,500 in scholarships to dozens of students pursuing degrees in science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) at colleges and universities across California and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) nationwide.

As communities celebrate National STEM Day on Nov. 8, the PG&E Foundation reaffirms its commitment to building tomorrow's workforce through investments in STEM education and scholarships.

This year, scholarships in the amounts of $2,500, $5,000 and $10,000 are being granted to 57 students from across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PG&E) service area through the program.

Since 2012, the Better Together STEM Scholarship Program has awarded nearly $8 million to accomplished students. This contribution is funded by PG&E shareholders and is not recovered through customer rates.

By investing in STEM education, the Foundation helps inspire curiosity, creativity, and innovation while empowering students to develop solutions and technologies that can make a positive impact in their hometown communities and beyond.

Scholarship recipients include Quennel Kempe of Fresno and Caden Kelly of Shingle Springs. Both students attend UC Berkeley. Kempe received a $5,000 scholarship and Kelly received a $2,500 scholarship.

"Receiving the PG&E STEM Scholarship shows me that my community believes in me. The financial assistance and encouragement give me the confidence to achieve my goals and make a greater impact in the future," said Kempe, who is studying computer science. 

"The PG&E STEM Scholarship has given me the freedom to focus fully on my education without the added stress of financial challenges. It also serves as a reminder of the values I want to carry forward, using my education to give back to my community, supporting others and helping make STEM opportunities more accessible for future generations," said Kelly who is studying electrical engineering.

Scholarships are based on academic achievement, demonstrated participation and leadership in school and community activities, and financial need. Recipients may reapply annually for up to five years.

Watch PG&E's video series of past STEM scholar recipients.

"We hope these students discover a path in science, technology, engineering, and math that not only leads to new innovations and breakthroughs but also brings them fulfillment and a sense of purpose. We are proud to support them on their journey as they pursue their higher education goals and dreams," said Carla Peterman, President, PG&E Corporation, and Chair of The PG&E Corporation Foundation Board.

Scholarship recipients must plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study for the entire 2026-2027 academic year and pursue their first undergraduate degree at an accredited four-year institution in California. HBCU eligibility was recently added after an increasing number of applicants were admitted to historically Black colleges and universities, none of which are in California.

Employees Supporting Local Scholars

In addition to the Better Together STEM Scholarship Program, PG&E's 11 employee resource groups (ERGs) and three engineering networking groups (ENGs) award scholarships to help offset the cost of higher education. The funds are raised entirely from employee contributions through direct donations, fundraising events and the company's employee giving program known as Campaign for the Community. Since 1989, more than $6 million ERG/ENG Scholarships has been raised and awarded to thousands of our hometown students.

About PG&E

Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of PG&E Corporation (NYSE: PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California. For more information, visit www.pge.com/ and http://www.pge.com/about/newsroom/.

The PG&E Corporation Foundation is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, separate from PG&E and sponsored by PG&E Corporation.

HCW11-040 was constructed with interleukin domains (IL-15 and IL-7) paired with a TGF-β trap, that in combination can potentially rejuvenate exhausted T cells for more effective cancer cell killing

HCW11-040 outperformed immune checkpoint inhibitors in converting immunological cold tumors to hot tumors for solid tumor immunotherapy in preclinical studies

MIRAMAR, Fla., Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HCW Biologics Inc. (the “Company” or “HCW Biologics”) (NASDAQ: HCWB), a U.S.-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company and leading developer in novel multi-functional fusion immunotherapeutics, for the treatment of autoimmune diseases, cancer, and senescence-associated dysplasia, announced the Company’s data update for HCW11-040 was selected as one of the Top 150 Abstracts by the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (“SITC”), out of 1,200 abstract submissions, for its scientific rigor, novelty, clarity, and potential impact on cancer immunotherapy. The Company will present the data update at the 41st Annual Meeting of SITC, taking place from November 4 – 8, 2026, in Phoenix, Arizona.

The Poster (Abstract #394), entitled, “A tetravalent, pembrolizumab-based fusion immunotherapeutic protein targeting exhausted T cells for expansion and activation,” will be presented during the Poster Session at the Poster Hall from 10 a.m.–2 p.m. MT and 6 – 8:10 p.m. MT, on Saturday, November 7.

HCW11-040 is a novel, first-in-class, fusion immunotherapeutic that is designed to block the checkpoint receptors and engage the costimulatory receptors, analogous to taking the foot off the brake and simultaneously hitting the gas. In preclinical studies, the blocking activity of PD1-PDL1 interaction demonstrated by HCW11-040 was comparable to pembrolizumab, a generic form of Keytruda®. HCW11-040 outperformed pembrolizumab in rejuvenating exhausted T cells against human cancer cells. HCW11-050, the mouse homologue of HCW11-040, was also shown to exhibit better anti-solid-tumor activities against cold tumors than immune checkpoint inhibitors in various relevant tumor efficacy preclinical models. It rejuvenated exhausted T cells and promoted T-cell infiltration into tumors to support cold-to-hot tumor conversion. Thus, HCW11-040 represents a novel cancer immunotherapeutic by combining immune checkpoint blockade with potent cytokine-mediated immune activation, enhancing CD8+ T-cell migration to tumors, and reducing immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment.

KEYTRUDA® is a registered trademark of Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC, a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc. and the company is not affiliated with HCWB.

HCW Biologics Inc. (the “Company”) (NASDAQ: HCWB) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformative fusion immunotherapeutics to treat diseases promoted by chronic inflammation, including autoimmune diseases, cancer, and senescence-associated dysplasia. HCW Biologics is the leader in creation of multi-valent immunotherapeutics with a unique protein-based scaffold, without the antibody Fc domain. The Company’s immunotherapeutics represent a new class of drugs that it believes have the potential to fundamentally change the treatment of proinflammatory and senescence-associated diseases and conditions that are promoted by chronic inflammation —and in doing so, improve patients’ quality of life and possibly extend longevity. A key aspect of the Company’s clinical development and financing strategy is to focus on its business development programs, including its commercial-ready reagents to be used in the production of immunotherapeutics for cancer and infectious diseases. data.title: New phase 2 data highlight the strength of the immune response induced by personalized cancer vaccine EVX-01 | EVAX Stock News
data.description:

  • Detection of neoantigen-specific T cells directly ex vivo indicates strong EVX-01-induced immune responses
  • Data further underlines the strong predictive performance of Evaxion’s AI-Immunology™ platform
  • The new biomarker data supplements recently published three-year data showing 89% vaccine target precision and sustained T-cell and clinical responses

COPENHAGEN, Denmark, November 6, 2026 - Evaxion A/S (NASDAQ: EVAX) (“Evaxion”), a clinical-stage TechBio company developing novel immunotherapies with its pioneering AI-Immunology™ platform, announces new biomarker data from its phase 2 trial with personalized cancer vaccine EVX-01 in patients with advanced melanoma (skin cancer).

The data demonstrate potent EVX-01 induced immune responses and further underline the strong predictive performance of Evaxion’s AI-Immunology™ platform. It will be presented in both an oral and a poster session today and tomorrow respectively at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) 2026 Annual Meeting, taking place in Phoenix, Arizona.

“It is exciting to announce yet another set of new and promising data providing insights into the magnitude, quality and systemic impact of EVX-01-induced immunity in advanced melanoma. The data provide a clear demonstration of the very strong immune responses induced by EVX-01 and also validates our AI-Immunology™ platform further. We are looking forward to sharing and discussing this data with both scientific stakeholders and potential business partners at the important SITC meeting”, says Birgitte Rønø, CSO and COO of Evaxion.

Comprehensive data package
The new data adds to EVX-01’s already comprehensive data package which includes three-year clinical response and immune data presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 held in October. These data showed 89% vaccine target precision and sustained T-cell and clinical responses at three-year follow-up in the phase 2 trial.

New findings include detection of EVX-01 induced neoantigen-specific T-cells directly ex vivo, which is a clear testament to the magnitude of the vaccine-induced immune responses. Ex vivo responses were dominated by CD4+ T-cells, while CD8+ T-cell responses were observed in half of patients.   

The data also documents a significant association (p<0.001) between predictions by AI-Immunology™ and actual T-cell responses, confirming the strong predictive performance of the platform. Essentially, the platform predicts, with very high precision, which neoantigens will illicit the strongest immune responses allowing for selection of these as optimal vaccine targets.

SITC oral and poster presentation details:

  • Abstract title: EVX-01 personalized AI-designed vaccine plus pembrolizumab induce neoantigen-specific T-cell responses and systemic immune modulation in advanced melanoma
  • Abstract#: 502

Oral presentation:

  • Session: 105b: Rapid Oral - Clinical 1
  • Location: Phoenix Convention Center, West Building-300 Level - 301BC
  • Date/Time: Friday, November 6, 2026, 12:30-1:30pm MT / 20.30-21.30 CET
  • Presenter:  Mads Lausen, Senior Scientist at Evaxion

Poster presentation:

  • Session: Poster Session
  • Location: Phoenix Convention Center, North Building-Lower Level - Exhibition Halls 4-6
  • Date/Time: Saturday, November 7, 2026, 12:30-1:30pm & 6:40-8:10pm MT / 20:30-21:30 CET & 02:40-04:10 CET (Sunday, November 8)
  • Presenter: Mads Lausen, Senior Scientist at Evaxion

About the phase 2 trial
The phase 2 trial investigated EVX-01 in patients with advanced melanoma (skin cancer). Each patient enrolled in the trial received a unique vaccine designed with Evaxion’s AI-Immunology™ prediction platform and manufactured based on their individual biology.

At two-year follow-up, the trial demonstrated an Objective Response Rate (ORR) of 75% as 12 out of 16 patients had objective clinical responses, with four patients obtaining a complete response. Clinical and T-cell responses were sustained at three-year follow-up. 89% of the EVX-01 neoantigen targets triggered a tumor-specific immune response in the patients.

In the first two-years, patients received EVX-01 in combination with MSD’s (Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA) anti-PD-1 therapy, KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab). In the third year, a subset of patients received EVX-01 as stand-alone therapy. KEYTRUDA® is a registered trademark of Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC, a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA.

About EVX-01
EVX-01 is a personalized peptide-based cancer vaccine intended for first-line treatment of multiple advanced solid cancer tumors. It is currently being evaluated as a treatment of advanced melanoma and is Evaxion’s lead clinical asset.

Designed with our AI-Immunology™ platform, EVX-01 is tailored to target the unique tumor profile and immune characteristics of each patient. It engages the patient's immune system by mounting a targeted response against tumor-specific neoantigens.

TORONTO, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hudbay Minerals Inc. (“Hudbay” or the “Company”) (TSX, NYSE: HBM) today announced that, further to the Company’s news release dated September 28, 2026, the Company has filed a National Instrument 43-101 technical report for its Snow Lake operations in Manitoba (the “2026 Technical Report”).

Hudbay’s 100% owned Snow Lake operations in Manitoba include the Lalor gold-copper-zinc mine, the New Britannia gold mill, the Stall base metals concentrator, the 1901 zinc-gold deposit, several satellite deposits and the former producing New Britannia gold mine currently on care and maintenance.

As disclosed in the September 28, 2026 news release, the highlights of the 2026 Technical Report include:

  • An enhanced gold production profile with a 37% increase in gold production over the next five yearsi.
  • Total life-of-mine gold production increased by 60% to 2.8 million ounces compared to 1.8 million ounces in the 2021 technical reporti.
  • The updated mine plan maintains average annual production of 185,000 ounces of gold over the next five yearsi reflecting several optimization initiatives including higher mill throughput at New Britannia and higher gold recoveries at the Stall mill to better utilize the combined 6,300 tonnes per day of processing capacity. Snow Lake’s proven and probable reserve mine life is extended to 2043.
  • Mineral reserve estimates increased to 27 million tonnes containing 2.0 million ounces of gold, representing a 38% increase in tonnage from the January 1, 2026 mineral reserve estimate. The increase in reserves and mine life extension is driven by reserve conversion at Lalor and 1901, higher reserves at the WIM and 3 Zone satellite deposits, and the first reserve estimate for the Talbot and Rail satellite deposits.
  • Life-of-mine plan is based on reserve estimates and reflects a conservative view based on Hudbay’s historical high resource-to-reserve conversion rate of 90%ii.

A copy of the 2026 Technical Report will be available on Hudbay’s corporate website at www.hudbay.com, Hudbay’s SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca and on Hudbay’s EDGAR profile at www.sec.gov.

Qualified Person and NI 43-101

The 2026 Technical Report is titled “National Instrument 43-101 Technical Report, Lalor and Snow Lake Operations, Manitoba, Canada”, with an effective date of September 1, 2026.

The technical and scientific information in this news release has been approved by Marc-André Brulotte, P. Geo., Executive Director, Global Mineral Resource Evaluation. Mr. Brulotte is a qualified person pursuant to National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”).

The 2026 Technical Report has been prepared pursuant to NI 43-101 under the supervision of Mr. Brulotte. It constitutes the current technical report in respect of Hudbay’s Snow Lake operations and supersedes and replaces all prior technical reports relating to the Snow Lake operations.

KEARNEYSVILLE, W.Va., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- West Virginia American Water is moving forward with additional upgrades to Jefferson County's water infrastructure with work to prepare the future site of the Central Grove Water Treatment Plant.

The project is located near the intersection of Goldenrod Drive and Marie Drive. Initial work includes selective tree clearing, grading, decorative fencing, landscaping improvements, and well evaluation.

The new water treatment plant will become part of the larger water system serving the area and represents an important step toward connecting the Mountain and Walnut Grove water systems. The Walnut Grove system already operates as an interconnected network of water treatment facilities. Its nine water treatment plants collectively serve approximately 4,960 active customers. Adding the Central Grove Water Treatment Plant to this system allows operators greater flexibility to manage the system, balance changing needs and continue to support reliable water service across the communities they serve.

"This project is about more than adding a new facility. It's another step toward a stronger, more connected water system," said Scott Wyman, President of West Virginia American Water. "Connecting different parts of the system gives our operators more flexibility and ways to support continued reliable water service for the communities we serve."

Since becoming the water and wastewater service provider for five acquired local utility entities in Jefferson County, West Virginia American Water has continued working to strengthen the local infrastructure that customers rely on every day. So far, the company has invested more than $11.7 million in local water and wastewater system improvements during its first three years of ownership. The Central Grove project builds upon that work by investing not only in individual facilities, but also in how different parts of the local water system can work together.

During this first phase, nearby residents may notice crews and equipment as the site is prepared for future construction. The work will also include landscaping improvements, reseeding and new trees. The Company encourages residents to stay out of work zones to maintain the safety for both the community and crews.

About American Water

With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders.

AMSTERDAM and PHILADELPHIA, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Akzo Nobel N.V. (AKZA; AKZOY) (“AkzoNobel”) and Axalta Coating Systems Ltd. (NYSE:AXTA) (“Axalta”) today received conditional approval from the European Commission for their proposed all-stock merger of equals, which will create a premier global coatings company. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027 subject to pending regulatory approvals.

Following constructive discussions with the European Commission, AkzoNobel and Axalta have agreed to a targeted remedy involving the divestment of AkzoNobel’s European vehicle refinish business.

The commitments offered fully address the preliminary competition concerns identified by the European Commission by removing the horizontal overlap between the companies' activities in the European Economic Area, UK and Switzerland. No other competition issues were identified by the European Commission in any other markets. This outcome will preserve the same level of competition and customer choice in the vehicle refinish coatings market in Europe while maintaining the strategic benefits of the merger on the overall deal.

The combination will bring together two leading coatings companies with complementary portfolios, technologies and brands, creating a global coatings company with approximately $17 billion in revenue and a broad portfolio across Powder Coatings, Aerospace Coatings, Refinish, Mobility, Marine and Protective Coatings, Industrial Coatings and Decorative Coatings.

“Receiving the European Commission’s approval is an important milestone as we move closer to completing our merger with Axalta,” says Greg Poux-Guillaume, CEO of AkzoNobel, who will serve as CEO of the combined company. “We’re well on track and look forward to bringing together our complementary technologies, expertise and talented teams to accelerate growth.”

Chris Villavarayan, Axalta CEO and President, who will serve as Deputy CEO of the combined company, adds: “We are pleased that the European Commission has approved the transaction. data.description:
Royal Caribbean Group (RCL) brand Silversea opened The Cormorant at 55 South in Puerto Williams, Chile, on November 5.

Silversea celebrates the opening of the 150-room hotel in Puerto Williams, Chile, with a ribbon-cutting ceremony featuring performances by local children and artists  

MIAMI, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Silversea, the leading experiential luxury and expedition travel brand, has officially opened The Cormorant at 55 South, a new 150-room hotel in Puerto Williams, Chile, the southernmost city on Earth. Marking a historic moment for the brand and a first-of-its-kind venture for Silversea and Royal Caribbean Group, the hotel opened with a ribbon-cutting ceremony on November 5, featuring Silversea executive leadership, Chilean national and regional authorities, and members of the local community. Developed in partnership with a consortium of Chilean investors, the hotel reflects the region it calls home while acting as the new gateway to Silversea's Antarctica Fly Cruise program. Every guest on the Antarctica Fly Cruise expedition will now arrive in Puerto Williams on a Silversea-branded charter flight and stay at The Cormorant, before continuing their journey to the Last Continent.

"Today marks a defining moment for Silversea," said Bert Hernandez, president, Silversea. "We opened The Cormorant at 55 South to make the journey to Antarctica easier and more comfortable for our guests. Now the expedition begins here, in a hotel designed around Puerto Williams, with the same service our guests expect while on board our ships. Silversea has always been about going further, and this is another example of how we are continuing to invest in the guest experience."

A FIRST FOR SILVERSEA AT THE SOUTHERN EDGE OF THE WORLD

The Cormorant carries on the leadership Silversea established in 2008, when it pioneered luxury expedition cruising, from the ship to the shore. Staffed by a team trained through The Silversea Way, Silversea's service culture, the hotel brings the brand's personalized service to the first welcome in Puerto Williams, and it was built to the standard guests expect on board. Built using modular construction, each of the 150 rooms were built in Mendoza, Argentina, and transported across the Andes and Patagonia to its place at 55 degrees south.

Its architecture and interiors draw on the landscape, local traditions, and regional materials, and that sense of place extends through the experience. Three large-scale works by Chilean artists bring the landscape, geology, and ecology of the far south into the hotel, while food and beverage begin with the destination itself and are built around local ingredients.

THE START OF THE ANTARCTICA FLY CRUISE JOURNEY

Guests on an Antarctica Fly Cruise expedition fly non-stop from Silversea's private terminal in Santiago to Puerto Williams on Silversea-branded charter flights and stay at The Cormorant before and after their voyage. Inside, the design moves guests from water and darkness toward warmth, wood, and fire.

Each space is designed to bring the region to life, making the destination the very heart of the experience.

  • Latitude 55: Rooted in Chilean flavors, regional ingredients, and local culinary traditions – like the asado – The Cormorant's restaurant, Latitude 55, brings Chilean Patagonia, Tierra del Fuego, and Puerto Williams to the table. Menus start with what grows, grazes, and swims in the region, and dinner is served family-style, with large platters at the center of the table.
  • Bar Sur: The hotel's social center serves teas and small bites by day and Chilean wines and spirits in the evening, with a wine list that tours Chile from north to south. Calafate, a deep indigo native berry, anchors the cocktails alongside Chilean Pisco, a national spirit, in flavors that are tart, herbal, and warm, with a hint of smoke that echoes the asado fire. Other experiences include a guided Pisco journey led by the Bar Sur team and wine tastings led by the hotel's sommelier.
  • Fireplace: Inspired by the regional tradition of fire as a place for hospitality and storytelling, the Fireplace offers plush seating and expansive windows overlooking the Patagonian landscape.
  • Art and Design: Three large-scale works by Chilean artists anchor the interiors: Navarino, a steel sculpture by Paola Vezzani suspended in the main lobby; Dientes de Navarino, a bar mural by Cata Flaño; and La Memoria de las Piedras, an installation of seventy handcrafted ceramic stones by Javier Canales.
  • Outdoor Experiences: Guests can kayak the sheltered waters of the Beagle Channel, hike the shoreline trails of Seno Lauta, and explore the landscape on horseback, with plenty of chances to spot cormorants, dolphin gulls, and upland geese along the way.

OPENING DAY: A CEREMONY SHAPED BY PUERTO WILLIAMS

The grand opening of The Cormorant drew on the music, history, and community of Chile's far south.

Los Chamames de la Patagonia, a folk ensemble founded in Punta Arenas in 2015, performed a Patagonian chamamé with children from the local Grupo Folklorico. The musical tradition has Guaraní roots in northeastern Argentina and traveled south with seasonal workers, shepherds, and families. Local schoolchildren sang the Chilean national anthem, accompanied by young musicians.

The ribbon, featuring natural junco fibers handwoven by local artisans, featured a chain of interconnected circles that symbolize the connections between people, cultures, and territories, and a meeting point between Patagonia, its communities, and travelers from around the world. Specially designed links allowed the hotel's leaders and Chilean authorities to cut it together while the woven circles remained intact.

STARTING WITH 29 ANTARCTICA FLY CRUISE VOYAGES

The Cormorant represents a long-term investment in how Silversea delivers the Antarctica experience.

Through March 2027, Silver Endeavour, Silver Wind, and Silver Cloud will operate 40 voyages, including 29 Antarctica Fly Cruise voyages, each featuring a stay at The Cormorant at 55 South. The season's itineraries range from six to 21 nights and extend beyond the Antarctic Peninsula to South Georgia and the Falkland Islands.

For more information on The Cormorant at 55 South and Silversea's Antarctica Fly Cruise program, visit: https://www.silversea.com/the-cormorant-at-55-south.html

Find additional assets in our digital press kit: https://royalcaribbeangrouppresscenter.com/silversea/dpk/cormorant

About Silversea
Silversea is the leading experiential luxury and expedition travel brand, offering guests immersive experiences on all seven continents, personalized service, and an innovative culinary offering aboard its 12 intimate ocean and expedition ships. Silversea's itineraries encompass an unparalleled range of destinations worldwide, from the Mediterranean and the Caribbean to the Galápagos, both Polar Regions, and hundreds of fascinating places in between. Set to strengthen its destination leadership starting in 2026, the brand is developing the southernmost hotel on Earth, The Cormorant at 55 South, in Puerto Williams, Chile – offering guests a uniquely seamless journey to Antarctica. Silversea brings its like-minded guests closer to their destination in uncompromised comfort, championing the joy of travel, an enriching spirit of discovery, and an enduring commitment to Silversea's signature "To Finding More" promise. SEATTLE, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Perspective Therapeutics, Inc. (“Perspective,” the “Company,” “we,” “us,” and “our”) (NYSE AMERICAN: CATX), a radiopharmaceutical development company pioneering advanced systemic treatments for cancers, today announced updated interim monotherapy results from its ongoing Phase 1/2a clinical trial of [212Pb]lapemelanotide zapixetar (VMT01), an investigational targeted alpha therapy. The Company presented the data as a poster at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) 41st Annual Meeting, being held November 4 to 8, 2026, in Phoenix, Arizona.

The update covered 20 patients who received at least one monotherapy treatment of lapemelanotide as of September 18, 2026 (DCO date), across three dose cohorts of up to cumulative 4.5 mCi, 9 mCi, and 15 mCi, administered in three treatments of 1.5 mCi, 3.0 mCi, and 5.0 mCi, respectively, every eight weeks.

At the program’s focus dose of 3.0 mCi, two out of the eight patients enrolled in the monotherapy cohort had objective partial responses, one of whom remained in partial response and in study approximately 40 weeks after their first treatment. The disease control rate (DCR) was 75%, including two patients with long-lasting disease stabilization. As of the DCO date, eight patients had received at least one treatment in this dose cohort, with the eighth patient recently treated and not yet eligible for their first tumor assessment.

Across all 20 monotherapy patients, no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), treatment-related serious treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), or adverse event-related treatment discontinuations were reported. Grade 3 or higher TEAEs occurred in five patients (25%), with none considered treatment-related.

“Despite significant advances in immunotherapy, many patients with advanced melanoma do not respond to checkpoint inhibitors, or they experience disease progression following treatment,” said Markus Puhlmann, MD, Perspective’s Chief Medical Officer. “The clinical activity observed with lapemelanotide, together with its safety profile to date, supports further investigation of targeted alpha therapy as a potential treatment option for patients with limited alternatives.”

“With lapemelanotide, we’re seeing responses and meaningful periods of disease stabilization in heavily pretreated patients,” said Thijs Spoor, Perspective’s Chief Executive Officer. “We believe there is an opportunity to make a difference for these patients. We’re continuing to learn from the data as we determine the best way to move the program forward.”

Perspective designed lapemelanotide to target and deliver 212Pb to metastatic melanoma tumor sites expressing MC1R, a protein that can be overexpressed in metastatic melanoma tumors.1 The Company is conducting a multi-center, open-label dose escalation, dose expansion study (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05655312) in patients with histologically confirmed melanoma and MC1R-positive imaging scans obtained with the companion investigational imaging agent [203Pb]VMT01.

– Zero HIV Acquisitions Occurred Among Participants Receiving Twice-Yearly Lenacapavir During the 52-Week Study Period –

– PURPOSE 5 Study Findings Highlight the Potential of Long-Acting HIV Prevention Option to Address Persistence Challenges with Up to a Full Year of Protection After Second Dose –

FOSTER CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced results from the PURPOSE 5 trial showing significantly higher persistence—defined as consistent and continuous on-time use—among people starting twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir for HIV prevention as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), compared with those starting daily oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (F/TDF). The trial included people in the United Kingdom (UK) and France who would benefit from PrEP. These data will be presented at HIV Glasgow 2026.

Key Highlights:

  • Twice-yearly lenacapavir achieved significantly higher one-year PrEP persistence than daily oral F/TDF, with 85.6% of participants receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir remaining persistent through Week 52 compared with 46.3% for participants taking once-daily F/TDF (p<0.0001).
  • PURPOSE 5 is the first randomized study specifically designed to compare persistence between a long-acting HIV prevention option and daily oral PrEP among individuals not currently taking PrEP.
  • Zero HIV acquisitions occurred among participants receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir during the 52-week study period.
  • Results highlight the potential of twice-yearly lenacapavir to address persistence challenges that can limit the effectiveness of HIV prevention efforts.

Despite substantial progress in HIV prevention, approximately 1.2 million people acquired HIV globally in 2025, according to UNAIDS, underscoring the need for prevention options that better support long-term use and protection. Persistence on PrEP remains one of the most important determinants of real-world prevention effectiveness. Daily oral F/TDF is currently the most commonly used oral PrEP medication globally.

“While starting on PrEP is important, persisting on PrEP is critical to preventing HIV acquisition,” said Professor Chloe Orkin, MBE, Clinical Professor of Infection and Inequities, Queen Mary University of London. “In PURPOSE 5, people in France and the United Kingdom receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir injections were much more likely to keep taking PrEP effectively compared with those receiving daily PrEP tablets. These findings suggest long-acting injections for PrEP may help address a very important barrier to sustained HIV prevention for people who need it. It is notable that the study was able to reach a high proportion of new PrEP users.”

“This study was designed specifically to evaluate one of the most important challenges in HIV prevention today: helping people remain on PrEP for as long as they need protection,” said Jared Baeten, MD, PhD, Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, Virology Therapeutic Area Head, Gilead Sciences. “These results demonstrate that twice-yearly lenacapavir has the potential to help close the gap between starting PrEP and staying on PrEP which can have an important impact on our efforts to end the HIV epidemic in Europe and around the world.”

PURPOSE 5 Results

PURPOSE 5 is an ongoing Phase 2, randomized, open-label study evaluating PrEP persistence among individuals with HIV prevention needs in the United Kingdom and France who were not taking PrEP at the time of enrollment. Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive either twice-yearly lenacapavir or daily oral F/TDF and were followed for 52 weeks.

A total of 267 participants enrolled in the study, including cisgender men (72.3%), cisgender women (7.1%) and gender-diverse individuals (20.6%). 37.8% were PrEP-naïve at baseline.

At Week 52:

  • 85.6% (154/180) of participants receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir remained persistent on PrEP
  • 46.3% (37/80) of participants receiving daily oral F/TDF remained persistent on PrEP
  • The difference of 39.3 (95% CI: 26.66% - 51.41%) was statistically significant (p<0.0001)

Zero HIV acquisitions occurred among participants receiving lenacapavir. One HIV acquisition was reported in the F/TDF group; drug-level analysis at the time of diagnosis was consistent with fewer than two doses of F/TDF per week. Participant retention across both groups remained high throughout the study, with 89.4% of participants in the lenacapavir group and 83.9% of participants in the F/TDF group attending the Week 52 study visit.

For the purpose of this study Gilead used strict protocol definitions of persistence. For lenacapavir persistence was defined as receipt of on-time LEN injection at Day 1/baseline and week 26 (+/- 2 weeks) and on-time follow-up visit at week 52. For F/TDF persistence was defined as dried blood spot (DBS) tenofovir diphosphate (TFV-DP) concentrations consistent with ≥ 4 doses/week (≥ 700 fmol/punch) at Weeks 13, 26, 39, and 52.

Safety

The safety profile observed in PURPOSE 5 was generally consistent with previous studies of lenacapavir for HIV prevention. Serious adverse events were uncommon and occurred in 3.9% of participants receiving lenacapavir and 3.4% of participants receiving F/TDF. Investigators determined that no serious adverse events were related to study treatment. No participants discontinued treatment due to adverse events with lenacapavir. The most common treatment-related events were mild or moderate injection-site reactions (ISRs) associated with subcutaneous lenacapavir administration, and included nodules (67.8%), pain (60.0%), induration (20.6%), and erythema (17.8%).

Addressing a Critical HIV Prevention Challenge

Although awareness and availability of PrEP have increased, persistence remains a challenge across many settings. Daily oral PrEP is highly effective when taken as prescribed, but real-world studies have consistently shown that many individuals discontinue PrEP within the first year of use. By reducing dosing frequency to one dose every six months, twice-yearly lenacapavir has the potential to offer a discreet and convenient HIV prevention option that may better align with the needs and preferences of some individuals more vulnerable to HIV acquisition.

About PURPOSE 5

PURPOSE 5 is the first randomized study designed specifically to compare persistence between a long-acting injectable HIV prevention option and daily oral PrEP among individuals who would benefit from PrEP and were not currently taking oral PrEP. The Phase 2 study conducted in the United Kingdom and France evaluates whether twice-yearly lenacapavir can improve persistence compared with daily oral F/TDF over 52 weeks.

PURPOSE 5 is part of Gilead’s broader PURPOSE clinical development program evaluating lenacapavir across diverse populations and settings with the goal of expanding HIV prevention choice through long-acting prevention options.

About the PURPOSE Program

Gilead’s landmark PURPOSE program is the most comprehensive and diverse HIV prevention trial program ever conducted. The program comprises five HIV prevention trials around the world that are focused on innovation in science, trial design, community engagement, and health equity.

The PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2 trials evaluated the safety and efficacy of twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir to reduce the chance of getting HIV. The ongoing Phase 2 and 3 program, consisting of PURPOSE 1-5 studies, is assessing the potential of lenacapavir to help a diverse range of people around the world who could benefit from PrEP.

More information about the PURPOSE program, including individual trial descriptions, populations and locations, can be found at www.purposestudies.com.

About Lenacapavir

Twice-yearly lenacapavir is approved in multiple countries as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV in adults and adolescents who are at risk of HIV acquisition. Lenacapavir is also approved in multiple countries for the treatment of multi-drug-resistant HIV in adults, in combination with other antiretrovirals.

The multi-stage mechanism of action of lenacapavir is distinguishable from other currently approved classes of antiviral agents. While most antivirals act on just one stage of viral replication, lenacapavir is designed to inhibit HIV at multiple stages of its lifecycle and has no known cross resistance exhibited in vitro to other existing drug classes.

Lenacapavir is being evaluated as a long-acting option in multiple ongoing and planned early and late-stage clinical studies in Gilead’s HIV prevention and treatment research program, including a once-yearly injection for HIV prevention. Lenacapavir is being developed as a foundation for potential future HIV therapies with the goal of offering both long-acting oral and injectable options with several dosing frequencies, in combination or as a mono agent, that help address individual needs and preferences of people and communities affected by HIV. The journal Science named lenacapavir its 2024 “Breakthrough of the Year.”

Indication for Yeytuo® (lenacapavir)

Yeytuo injection is indicated in combination with safer sex practices for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 infection in adults and adolescents with increased HIV-1 acquisition risk weighing at least 35kg.

Indication for Yeztugo® (lenacapavir)

Yeztugo is indicated for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in adults and adolescents (≥35kg) who are at risk for HIV-1 acquisition. Individuals must have a negative HIV-1 test prior to initiating Yeztugo.

Important Safety Information for Yeztugo

BOXED WARNING: RISK OF DRUG RESISTANCE WITH USE OF YEZTUGO IN UNDIAGNOSED HIV-1 INFECTION

  • Individuals must be tested for HIV-1 infection prior to initiating Yeztugo, and with each subsequent injection of Yeztugo, using a test approved or cleared by the FDA for the diagnosis of acute or primary HIV-1 infection. Drug-resistant HIV-1 variants have been identified with use of Yeztugo by individuals with undiagnosed HIV-1 infection. Do not initiate Yeztugo unless negative infection status is confirmed. Individuals who acquire HIV-1 while receiving Yeztugo must transition to a complete HIV-1 treatment regimen.

Contraindications

  • Yeztugo is contraindicated in individuals with unknown or positive HIV-1 status.

Warnings and precautions

  • Comprehensive risk management:
    • Use Yeztugo to reduce the risk of HIV-1 acquisition as part of a comprehensive prevention strategy including adherence to the administration schedule and safer sex practices, including condoms, to reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
    • HIV-1 acquisition risk includes behavioral, biological, or epidemiologic factors including, but not limited to, condomless sex, past or present STIs, self-identified HIV risk, having sexual partners of unknown HIV-1 viremic status, or sexual activity in a high-prevalence area or network. Counsel individuals on the use of other prevention methods to help reduce their risk.
    • Use Yeztugo only in individuals confirmed to be HIV-1 negative. Evaluate for current or recent signs or symptoms consistent with HIV-1 infection. Confirm HIV-1 negative status prior to initiating, prior to each subsequent injection, and as clinically appropriate.
  • Potential risk of resistance:
    • There is a potential risk of developing resistance to Yeztugo if an individual acquires HIV-1 before or when receiving Yeztugo, or following discontinuation. HIV-1 resistance substitutions may emerge in individuals with undiagnosed HIV-1 infection taking only Yeztugo, because Yeztugo alone is not a complete regimen for HIV-1 treatment.
    • To minimize this risk, it is essential to test before each injection and additionally as clinically appropriate. Individuals confirmed to have HIV-1 must immediately begin a complete HIV-1 treatment regimen.
    • Alternative forms of PrEP should be considered after discontinuation of Yeztugo for those who are at continuing risk of HIV-1 acquisition and should be initiated within 28 weeks of the last Yeztugo injection.
  • Long-acting properties and potential associated risks:
    • Residual concentrations of Yeztugo may remain in systemic circulation for up to 12 months or longer after the last injection.
    • Select individuals who agree to the required injection dosing schedule because nonadherence or missed doses could lead to HIV-1 acquisition and development of resistance.
  • Serious injection site reactions: Improper administration (intradermal injection) has been associated with serious injection site reactions, including necrosis and ulcer. Only administer Yeztugo subcutaneously.

Adverse reactions

  • Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) in Yeztugo clinical trials were injection site reactions, headache, and nausea.

Drug interactions

  • Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers may significantly decrease Yeztugo concentrations. Dosage modifications are recommended when initiating these inducers.
  • It is not recommended to use Yeztugo with combined P-gp, UGT1A1, and strong CYP3A inhibitors.
  • Coadministration of Yeztugo with sensitive substrates of CYP3A or P-gp may increase their concentrations and result in the increased risk of their adverse events. Yeztugo may increase the exposure of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A initiated within 9 months after the last injection of Yeztugo.

Dosage and administration

  • HIV screening: Test for HIV-1 infection prior to initiating, prior to each subsequent injection, and as clinically appropriate using an approved or cleared test for the diagnosis of acute or primary HIV-1 infection.
  • Dosage: Initiation dosing (injections and tablets) followed by once-every-6-months continuation injection dosing. Tablets may be taken with or without food.
    • Initiation: Day 1: 927 mg by subcutaneous injection (2 x 1.5-mL injections) and 600 mg orally (2 x 300-mg tablets). Day 2: 600 mg orally.
    • Continuation: 927 mg by subcutaneous injection every 6 months (26 weeks) from date of last injection ±2 weeks.
  • Anticipated delayed injections: If scheduled 6-month injection is anticipated to be delayed by more than 2 weeks, Yeztugo tablets may be taken on an interim basis (for up to 6 months) until injections resume. Dosage is 300 mg orally (1 x 300-mg tablet) once every 7 days. Resume continuation injections within 7 days of the last oral dose.
  • Missed injections: If more than 28 weeks have elapsed since the last injection and Yeztugo tablets have not been taken, restart with initiation dosing if clinically appropriate.
  • Dosage modifications of Yeztugo are recommended when initiating with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers. Consult the full Prescribing Information for recommendations.

About Gilead HIV

For more than 35 years, Gilead has been a leading innovator in the field of HIV, driving advances in treatment, prevention and cure research. Gilead researchers have developed 14 HIV medications, including the first single-tablet regimen to treat HIV, the first antiretroviral for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to help reduce new HIV infections, and the first long-acting injectable HIV treatment medication administered twice-yearly. Our advances in medical research have helped to transform HIV into a treatable, preventable, chronic condition for millions of people.

Gilead is committed to continued scientific innovation to provide solutions for the evolving needs of people affected by HIV around the world. Through partnerships, collaborations and charitable giving, the company also aims to improve education, expand access and address barriers to care, with the goal of ending the HIV epidemic worldwide. Gilead has been repeatedly recognized as one of the top two leading philanthropic funders of HIV-related programs in a report released by Funders Concerned About AIDS.

Discover more about Gilead’s unique collaborations worldwide and the work to help end the HIV epidemic.

Gilead Sciences, Inc. is a biopharmaceutical company that has pursued and achieved breakthroughs in medicine for more than three decades, with the goal of creating a healthier world for all people. In 17 first-line patients treated with the combination, the estimated two-year overall survival (OS) rate was 70% - Median OS was not reached at a median follow-up of 29 months and 10 patients remained on study

Majority of patients (64%) with an OS over 2 years received only the combination

The combination achieved a 29% overall response rate with a median duration of response of 24 months and a 71% disease control rate

First data showing clinical activity and manageable safety profile with a combination of two T cell engagers in a solid tumor

The Company is planning a Phase 2/3 randomized trial evaluating the combination in unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma

(OXFORDSHIRE, England & RADNOR, PA & GAITHERSBURG, MD, US, November 6, 2026) Immunocore Holdings plc (Nasdaq: IMCR) (“Immunocore” or the “Company”), a commercial-stage biotechnology company pioneering and delivering transformative immunomodulating medicines to radically improve outcomes for patients with cancer, infectious diseases and autoimmune diseases, presented data from its Phase 1/2 trial evaluating brenetafusp alone and in combination with KIMMTRAK in HLA-A*02:01-positive patients with metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM), in a poster session at the 2026 Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) Annual Meeting. The data will also be presented in an oral session on Saturday, November 7, at 3:45 p.m. ET.

KIMMTRAK and brenetafusp are ImmTAC molecules targeting gp100 and PRAME, respectively, with PRAME representing an established negative prognostic factor in mUM. KIMMTRAK is the first bispecific T cell receptor therapy to demonstrate survival benefit in a solid tumor and is the standard of care for HLA-A*02:01-positive adults with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma. Brenetafusp is an investigational candidate being evaluated in a range of tumors, including first-line cutaneous melanoma in the PRISM-MEL-301 Phase 3 trial. Adding brenetafusp to KIMMTRAK tests the hypothesis of whether the combination may improve outcomes in patients with HLA-A*02:01-positive mUM by increasing target engagement and enhancing T cell-mediated tumor killing.

“Immunocore continues to lead bispecific T cell engager innovation, having demonstrated the first overall survival benefit in metastatic uveal melanoma. We are now seeing the synergistic potential of combining two clinically active ImmTAC therapies. The 1- and 2-year overall survival data could be practice-changing, and I look forward to evaluating this combination in a randomized trial for patients with metastatic uveal melanoma,” said Dr. Omid Hamid, Chief of Research & Immuno-Oncology, Co-Director, Cutaneous Malignancy Program at The Angeles Clinic & Research Institute.

“These encouraging Phase 1 data suggest combining brenetafusp with tebentafusp may offer a meaningful new option for HLA-A*02:01-positive patients with metastatic uveal melanoma,” said Dr. Mohammed Dar, Executive Vice President, Clinical Development and Chief Medical Officer of Immunocore. “Building on our leadership with KIMMTRAK, we believe that targeting both gp100 and PRAME – a combined ImmTAC approach – offers the potential to deliver an even greater benefit for HLA-A*02:01-positive patients.”

At the June 2026 data cut-off, 22 patients with mUM had received clinically active doses of brenetafusp monotherapy and 26 had received brenetafusp plus tebentafusp. The Company believes that this is the first data showing clinical activity and a manageable safety profile for a combination of two T cell engagers in a solid tumor.

Across the 17 evaluable first-line patients who received the combination, overall response rate (ORR) was 29% with a median duration of response (mDoR) of 24.1 months. The disease control rate (DCR) was 71% and median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 8.1 months. At the data cut-off, median overall survival (mOS) had not been reached at a median follow-up of 29 months. OS rates were 88% at one year and 70% at two years with 10 of the 17 patients remaining on study. The majority of patients with OS >2 years (64%; 7 out of 11) had received only the brenetafusp and tebentafusp combination.

In the 16 evaluable patients who received brenetafusp monotherapy in the second-line or later setting, ORR was 19%, mDoR 14.5 months, DCR 63%, mPFS 4.2 months, and mOS 20.3 months. OS rates were 63% at one year and 31% at two years.

The safety profile of brenetafusp as monotherapy and in combination with tebentafusp was generally well tolerated and consistent with that observed for the individual agents, with no new safety signals reported. The most frequent treatment-related adverse event (TRAE) was reversible and manageable cytokine release syndrome (CRS), observed in 77% of combination patients and 73% of monotherapy patients, with the majority being Grade 1 or 2 (no Grade 3/4 CRS for the combination and 5% Grade 3 CRS for brenetafusp monotherapy). Grade 3 or 4 TRAEs were reported in 38% of combination patients and 41% of monotherapy patients, with the most frequent being transient lymphocyte count decrease that resolved without intervention. No TRAE led to discontinuation or death in either group.

The data also demonstrated molecular responses for the combination. Out of the nine patients who were evaluable for ctDNA response, eight (89%) had a molecular response, and four (44%) achieved ctDNA clearance.

The Company is planning to start DUET-UVEAL, a randomized Phase 2/3 trial, to further evaluate the combination for the treatment of HLA-A*02:01-positive adults with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma.

The data presented at SITC come from an ongoing Phase 1/2 trial (NCT04262466; EudraCT 2019-004046-16) evaluating brenetafusp as monotherapy as well as in combination across a number of solid tumors, including HLA-A*02:01-positive patients with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma. Brenetafusp and tebentafusp were administered by weekly intravenous infusion with step-up dosing.

Presentation details

Title: Phase 1 evaluation of brenetafusp alone and in combination with tebentafusp in metastatic uveal melanoma (Abstract number: 1177)

Poster session: Poster Hall
Date and Time: Friday, November 6, 2026, 10:00 a.m. MST / 12:00 p.m. EST

###

About ImmTAC® molecules for cancer

Immunocore’s proprietary T cell receptor (TCR) technology generates a novel class of bispecific biologics called ImmTAC (Immune mobilizing monoclonal TCRs Against Cancer) molecules that are designed to redirect the immune system to recognize and kill cancer cells. ImmTAC molecules are soluble TCRs engineered to recognize intracellular cancer antigens with ultra-high affinity and selectively kill these cancer cells via an anti-CD3 immune-activating effector function. Based on demonstrated T cell infiltration into human tumors, the ImmTAC mechanism of action holds the potential to treat hematologic and solid tumors, regardless of mutational burden or immune infiltration, including tumors that are characterized as immune “cold” or having low mutation burden.

About the IMC-F106C-101 Phase 1/2 trial

IMC-F106C-101 is a first-in-human, Phase 1/2 dose escalation trial in patients with multiple solid tumors, including non-small cell lung and ovarian cancers, as well as uveal melanoma, evaluating brenetafusp both as monotherapy and in combination arms with standards-of-care. The Phase 1 dose escalation portion of the trial was designed to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD), as well as to evaluate the safety, preliminary anti-tumor activity and pharmacokinetics of IMC-F106C (brenetafusp) both as monotherapy and in combination with standards-of-care. Brenetafusp is a bispecific protein built on Immunocore’s ImmTAC technology, and the Company’s first molecule to target the PRAME antigen.

About Uveal Melanoma

Uveal melanoma is a rare and aggressive form of melanoma, which affects the eye. This is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults and up to 50% of people with uveal melanoma will eventually develop metastatic disease. Unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma typically has a poor prognosis and had no approved treatment until KIMMTRAK.

About PRISM-MEL-301 (NCT06112314) – Phase 3 trial with brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME-A02) in 1L advanced cutaneous melanoma

The Phase 3 registrational trial is enrolling HLA-A*02:01-positive patients with previously untreated, advanced or metastatic cutaneous melanoma, with randomization to brenetafusp 160 mcg + nivolumab or a control arm of either nivolumab or nivolumab + relatlimab. The primary endpoint of the trial is progression free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR), with secondary endpoints of overall survival (OS) and overall response rate (ORR).

About KIMMTRAK

KIMMTRAK is a novel bispecific protein comprised of a soluble T cell receptor fused to an anti-CD3 immune-effector function. KIMMTRAK specifically targets gp100, a lineage antigen expressed in melanocytes and melanoma.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), which may be serious or life-threatening, occurred in patients receiving KIMMTRAK. Monitor for at least 16 hours following first three infusions and then as clinically indicated. Manifestations of CRS may include fever, hypotension, hypoxia, chills, nausea, vomiting, rash, elevated transaminases, fatigue, and headache. CRS occurred in 89% of patients who received KIMMTRAK, with 0.8% being grade 3 or 4. Ensure immediate access to medications and resuscitative equipment to manage CRS. Ensure patients are euvolemic prior to initiating the infusions. Closely monitor patients for signs or symptoms of CRS following infusions of KIMMTRAK. Monitor fluid status, vital signs, and oxygenation level and provide appropriate therapy. Withhold or discontinue KIMMTRAK depending on persistence and severity of CRS.

Skin Reactions

Skin reactions, including rash, pruritus, and cutaneous edema occurred in 91% of patients treated with KIMMTRAK. Monitor patients for skin reactions. If skin reactions occur, treat with antihistamine and topical or systemic steroids based on persistence and severity of symptoms. Withhold or permanently discontinue KIMMTRAK depending on the severity of skin reactions.

Elevated Liver Enzymes

Elevations in liver enzymes occurred in 65% of patients treated with KIMMTRAK. Monitor alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and total blood bilirubin prior to the start of and during treatment with KIMMTRAK. Withhold KIMMTRAK according to severity.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity

KIMMTRAK may cause fetal harm. Advise pregnant patients of potential risk to the fetus and patients of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with KIMMTRAK and 1 week after the last dose.

The most common adverse reactions (≥30%) in patients who received KIMMTRAK were cytokine release syndrome, rash, pyrexia, pruritus, fatigue, nausea, chills, abdominal pain, edema, hypotension, dry skin, headache, and vomiting. The most common (≥50%) laboratory abnormalities were decreased lymphocyte count, increased creatinine, increased glucose, increased AST, increased ALT, decreased hemoglobin, and decreased phosphate.

For more information, please see full Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) or full U.S. Prescribing Information (including BOXED WARNING for CRS).

About Immunocore

Immunocore is a commercial-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of a novel class of TCR bispecific immunotherapies called ImmTAX – Immune mobilizing monoclonal TCRs Against X disease – designed to treat a broad range of diseases, including cancer, autoimmune diseases and infectious diseases. Leveraging its proprietary, flexible, off-the-shelf ImmTAX platform, Immunocore is developing a deep pipeline in multiple therapeutic areas, including clinical and pre-clinical programs in oncology, infectious diseases, and autoimmune diseases. The Company’s most advanced oncology TCR therapeutic, KIMMTRAK, has been approved for the treatment of HLA-A*02:01-positive adult patients with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma in 39 countries, including the United States, European Union, Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom.

TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Canadian pension plan returns fell in the third quarter, mostly a result of rising bond yields, with the median pension plan returning -1.5% for the quarter ending September 30 and 4.4% year-to-date, according to the Northern Trust Canada Universe.

Third-quarter financial markets were shaped by the return of energy-driven inflation and a sharp rise in global interest rates. Middle East tensions returned to the foreground, pushing Brent crude oil above $100 per barrel and renewing concerns around inflation and energy supply. The rise in oil occurred against a backdrop of resilient economic activity and generally constructive corporate earnings. After holding rates in July, the U.S. Federal Reserve raised its policy rate by 25 basis points in September. The European Central Bank and Bank of Japan also adjusted policy rates higher during the month, while the Bank of Canada and Bank of England maintained their policy rates throughout the quarter. Meanwhile, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose more than 80 basis points to 5.29%, while sovereign yields also moved materially higher in Europe, the U.K. and Japan.

Despite this challenging backdrop, global equities, as measured by the MSCI ACWI Index, rose 1.8% in CAD (1.7% in USD) during the third quarter. Strong corporate earnings and resilient economic growth supported markets, while continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) remained an important driver of sentiment.

“Canadian pension plans navigated a complex market environment in the third quarter, as resilient equity markets were offset by the impact of rising bond yields,” said Katie Pries, Country Executive for Northern Trust Asset Servicing in Canada. “The quarter underscores how shifts in interest rates and inflation expectations can meaningfully influence pension portfolio performance, reinforcing the importance of maintaining a long-term perspective through changing market conditions.”

The Northern Trust Canada Universe tracks the performance of Canadian institutional defined benefit plans that subscribe to performance measurement services as part of Northern Trust’s asset servicing offerings.

In equity markets, U.S. stocks advanced on robust earnings and ongoing AI-related spending, while Japanese equities were among the strongest performers, benefiting from earnings growth and corporate governance reforms. Emerging markets lagged developed markets as semiconductor and memory-related stocks in Korea weakened following strong first-half gains. European equities underperformed amid weaker earnings momentum and higher interest rates, while UK equities benefited from greater exposure to energy and financials sectors.

Global bonds, as represented by the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index, fell -2.4% in CAD (-2.5% in USD) during the quarter as resilient economic activity, rising energy prices and persistent inflation concerns pushed bond yields higher across most developed markets. Markets also adjusted to expectations for further policy tightening, while increased sovereign issuance and corporate borrowing contributed to upward pressure on yields. Longer-dated government bonds underperformed as yields rose, while investment grade credit generated negative returns despite generally resilient corporate fundamentals. High yield bonds were down globally but proved relatively resilient, supported by higher income and lower interest-rate sensitivity.

  • Canadian equities, as represented by the S&P/TSX Composite Index, returned 1.6% in CAD (1.5% in USD) during the third quarter. Headline inflation was 3.1% at September quarter-end, up from 3.0% the prior month, remaining below the recent peak of 3.2%.
  • U.S. equities, as measured by the S&P 500 Index, gained 2.4% in CAD (2.3% in USD) against a backdrop of higher energy prices, rising yields and uncertainty regarding inflation.
  • International equity markets, as measured by the MSCI EAFE Index, had a gross return of 0.9% in CAD (0.9% in USD) in Q3.
  • During the third quarter, emerging markets (“EM”), as measured by the MSCI EM Index, had a gross decline of -0.2% in CAD (-0.2% in USD).

Canada’s economy showed more resilience than anticipated, yet inflation concerns and higher global bond yields gained prominence by September as trade tensions with the U.S. intensified. The Bank of Canada maintained its policy rate throughout the quarter, balancing largely contained inflation against uncertainty in the outlook arising from trade disputes. The main inflation risks now stem from supply conditions. Higher energy costs and additional tariffs, alongside potential disruptions to global supply chains, could lift prices temporarily across certain sectors.

The Canadian fixed income market, as measured by the FTSE Canada Universe Bond Index, fell -3.0% in CAD (-3.0% in USD). Provincial Bonds fell -4.1% while Federal and Corporate Bonds fell -2.6% and -2.1% respectively. Performance weakened with duration, as Short-, Mid- and Long-term bonds returned -0.9%, -3.0%, and -6.3%, respectively.

U.S. equity performance was largely driven by the energy sector as oil and gas prices surged over global supply concerns following escalating conflict in the Middle East. Information technology also benefitted owing to a shift from semiconductors to software and hyperscalers. As was widely anticipated, the Federal Reserve (“Fed”) unanimously voted to increase its key rate for the first time since July 2023 by 25 basis points, bringing it to a 3.75%-4% range, to tackle inflation brought on by rising oil and gasoline prices owing to the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh noted that while the economy, including the labour market, was strong, inflation had been “too high…for too long”, stating that the rate hike would support a “timelier return” to the bank’s 2 percent target. The dot-plot of officials’ expectations pointed to another 25bps rate hike this year, with some participants seeing the possibility for two. The inflation rate rose to 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in each of the previous two months and above the expected 3.6% largely resulting from higher energy prices.

The European Central Bank (“ECB”) raised its rates by a quarter point, lifting the deposit rate to 2.5%, its second hike since June, citing inflationary pressures, largely driven by higher oil and gas prices because of renewed fighting around the Strait of Hormuz, constraining crude supply. The bank expressed concern that the surge could translate into higher transport costs and costly heating for properties and noted that food inflation was also likely to rise. The bank also raised its forecast for eurozone growth from 0.8% to 0.9% in 2026. For the sixth time in a row, the Bank of England (“BoE”) held rates steady at 3.75%, in September, as a surge in energy prices pressures inflation. The BoE did however note that it would raise rates if high energy prices persist. The bank also raised its forecast for inflation, stating it would be “slightly above 4%” starting next year. The Bank of Japan raised its interest rates in September to 1.25%, the highest level in 31 years, in an effort to contain inflation resulting from rising energy costs. Governor Ueda noted that the bank’s focus has shifted to guarding against an inflation overshoot as domestic inflation exceeds the 2% target.

Emerging markets produced mixed results during the quarter. The People’s Bank of China left its one- and five-year loan prime rate (LPR) at 3.0% and 3.5%, respectively, for the 16th straight month reflecting caution amid Middle East-related uncertainty. Industrial production strengthened; export activity remained supported by AI-demand while retail sales softened. The Central Bank of Brazil cut its rate to 13.75% noting an uncertain environment due to conflict in the Middle East and monetary policy decisions in advanced economies while domestically data showed a moderation in economic activity and an ease in inflation. The Reserve Bank of India held rates at 5.25%, balancing resilient domestic growth against evolving inflationary and global risks.
